subject: Sizing for AuroraTek reserved fleet — traffic orthogonalization, KV-cache impact & SLA asks
messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@auroratek.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: platform@auroratek.com
Date: 2026-05-17 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing for AuroraTek reserved fleet — initial data attached

Hi Tessa / Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on. We're moving toward a reserved GPU commitment for our inference tier and want Redwood's sizing guidance so we commit the right capacity. I attached a short sample of last week's traffic (auroratek_traffic_sample.csv) and a handful of canonical prompts (prompt_samples.txt). A few quick context points: 
- We expect an average of ~12k requests/day to start, with heavy weekday spikes (potential 5x) for our search augmentation path.
- ~70% of requests are short retrieval-augmented prompts (avg prompt ~80 tokens, expected response ~60 tokens). The rest are longer generation flows (avg prompt 420 tokens, response ~350 tokens).
- Majority of calls use streaming but we have some batch-style synchronous calls during nightly processing.

Questions we have:
1) How much difference does prefix KV-caching make for our mix?
2) How should we think about P99 latency SLOs vs commit sizing for burst windows?
3) Any particular tokenization/quantization choices you'd recommend given mixed short/long distribution?

Happy to hop on a 30-min call but wanted to give the raw artifacts first.

Thanks,
Rajiv Menon
Head of Platform, AuroraTek
Attachments: auroratek_traffic_sample.csv (csv, 42KB); prompt_samples.txt (txt, 4KB)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@auroratek.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-17 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing for AuroraTek reserved fleet — initial data attached

Hi Rajiv — thanks for the artifacts, this is exactly what we need to start. Quick follow-ups so we can produce a concrete sizing + SLA tradeoff table before a call: 

1) Average and 95th percentile response token counts by prompt class (short retrieval vs long generation). If you can add pctiles to the CSV that helps.
2) Which endpoints use streaming vs non-streaming (list of route names or API paths is fine).
3) Desired P50/P95/P99 latency targets for the user-facing endpoint(s) and the nightly batch window.
4) Are you expecting a monthly reserved commit (baseline) with burst pool or a strict steady commit?
5) Any regulatory constraints for on-prem/private routing or strict isolation?

If you prefer, we can send a short matrix to fill (we can seed it with guesses from the sample). We can also run a quick micro-benchmark with the sample prompts to estimate KV-cache hit uplift and token-cost delta. 

Suggested next step: if you can give quick answers above and drop a one-week telemetry export (if available) we'll produce a preliminary sizing matrix + recommended GPU mix and quantization profile by EOD Tue. Otherwise I can schedule a 30-min sync.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0134
Attachments referenced: none
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-17 12:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: quick sizing hypotheses for AuroraTek (notes)

Tessa / Marissa — internal notes before we respond back to Rajiv with a seeded matrix. Pulling estimates from the sample:
- Baseline QPS estimate (weekday): ~0.6–0.9 req/s sustained, with 3–5 req/s peaks in high-traffic windows (matches 5x spikes Rajiv mentioned).
- Mixed token distribution implies KV-cache will help heavily for the short retrieval paths — expect 3x token savings on those requests if we can cache prefixes and reuse KV. For long generation flows, KV-cache impact negligible.
- If they want P99 < 250ms for the short retrieval route, we'll likely need a mix of reserved GPUs sized for peak occupancy with oversubscription guardrail ~1.2x; otherwise P99 will drift.
- Suggested quantization: 4-bit (nf4) for long generations if output quality tolerates it; int8/4-bit hybrid for retrieval model variants to reduce memory and increase concurrent slots.

Ask we should surface to Rajiv to make sizing deterministic: 1) one-week telemetry export (per-route qps and token histograms), 2) confirmation on commit model (monthly reserved vs flexible), 3) expected growth horizon (3 months / 12 months). I can seed a GPU-mix table (A100/4-slot eqv vs H100/6-slot eqv) once we have token pctiles.

-karthik
Principal Pre-Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@auroratek.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, platform@auroratek.com
Date: 2026-05-17 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing for AuroraTek reserved fleet — initial data attached

Hi Tessa,

Thanks — answers inline below and I attached a larger export (telemetry_week1_export.json).

1) Token pctiles: Short retrieval prompts — avg 82 tokens, p95 210, p99 380. Long generation prompts — avg 432 tokens, p95 890, p99 1,350. (See telemetry export).
2) Streaming routes: /api/v1/search_stream, /api/v1/assist_stream (approx 68% of traffic). Non-streaming: /api/v1/summarize, /api/v1/batch_gen.
3) Latency targets: user-facing search_stream — target P50 80ms, P95 160ms, P99 280ms. Nightly batch — best-effort, under two-minute walltime preferred.
4) Commit model: looking for a monthly reserved baseline with a burst pool. We want guidance on the sizing that minimizes cost while hitting the P99 target for search_stream.
5) No special regulatory routing required for this rollout.

We can hop on a 30-min call Wed 10am PT if that helps — otherwise feel free to seed the matrix and we'll review.

Appended: telemetry_week1_export.json (json, 1.7MB)

Best,
Rajiv
